shortDescription: Retrieve information about one or more oVirt/RHV virtual machines

options.name: all_content
options.description: If I(true) all the attributes of the virtual machines should be included in the response.

options.name: auth
options.description: Dictionary with values needed to create HTTP/HTTPS connection to oVirt:

options.name: case_sensitive
options.description: If I(true) performed search will take case into account.

options.name: current_cd
options.description: If I(true) it will get from all virtual machines current attached cd.

options.name: fetch_nested
options.description: If I(yes) the module will fetch additional data from the API. It will fetch only IDs of nested entity. It doesn't fetch multiple levels of nested attributes. Only the attributes of the current entity. User can configure to fetch other attributes of the nested entities by specifying C(nested_attributes). This parameter is deprecated and replaced by C(follow).

options.name: follow
options.description: List of linked entities, which should be fetched along with the main entity. This parameter replaces usage of C(fetch_nested) and C(nested_attributes). All follow parameters can be found at following url: https://ovirt.github.io/ovirt-engine-api-model/master/#types/vm/links_summary

options.name: max
options.description: The maximum number of results to return.

options.name: nested_attributes
options.description: Specifies list of the attributes which should be fetched from the API. This parameter apply only when C(fetch_nested) is I(true). This parameter is deprecated and replaced by C(follow).

options.name: next_run
options.description: Indicates if the returned result describes the virtual machine as it is currently running or if describes the virtual machine with the modifications that have already been performed but that will only come into effect when the virtual machine is restarted. By default the value is set by engine.

options.name: pattern
options.description: Search term which is accepted by oVirt/RHV search backend. For example to search VM X from cluster Y use following pattern: name=X and cluster=Y
